title: FAO Global Soil Organic Carbon Sequestration Potential Map (GSOCseq)
description: Global 30 arc-second (about 1 km) maps of the topsoil (0-30 cm) organic carbon sequestration potential of current agricultural land, produced by the FAO Global Soil Partnership from national submissions and GSP gap-filling. Layers include initial SOC stocks in 2020 (T0), SOC stocks projected for 2040 under business-as-usual (BAU) and three sustainable soil management scenarios (SSM1/2/3: +5, +10 and +20% carbon inputs), relative sequestration rates compared with BAU, and uncertainty layers.
purpose: Scenario-based indication of where improved management of Algerian cropland and grazing land could raise topsoil organic carbon, e.g. for carbon-farming, land restoration or NDC discussions.

license_notes: Unclear and conflicting. The FAO catalogue records for the global 1 km layers (e.g. 'GSOCseq - Relative soil organic carbon sequestration rates (Global - 1 km)', edition 'Version 2.0', 2025-01-07) carry the licence tag CC-BY-SA-4.0, but their resource-constraints text reads 'Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)'. Older catalogue records for the same layers (2022) are tagged CC-BY-4.0 with no constraint text. This record uses the most restrictive stated terms (non-commercial, share-alike) until FAO clarifies; confirm with the GSP Secretariat before commercial use.

spatial_extent.description: Global, but only on current agricultural land as defined by the GSOCseq land-use input, at 0-30 cm. Algeria is included as a 'Gap-filling Layer' (GSOCseq v1.1 report, Annex A3). On a 1-degree grid inside Algeria the 2020 SOC stock layer (SOCS T0X) had values at 5.2% of points: 21.6% north of 32 N, 0% further south. Values exist only on agricultural pixels of the north.

temporal_extent.description: Baseline SOC stocks represent 2020 (T0). Scenario layers are projections for 2040, after 20 years of BAU or SSM management. These are model projections, not observations.

variables.name: SOCS BAU, SSM1, SSM2, SSM3
variables.description: Projected SOC stock 0-30 cm in 2040 under business-as-usual and +5/+10/+20% carbon-input scenarios

variables.name: RSR SSM1, SSM2, SSM3
variables.description: Relative sequestration rate: mean annual SOC stock change over 20 years under SSM compared with BAU

variables.name: Uncertainty layers
variables.description: Separate FAO catalogue records for projected-stock and RSR uncertainties (Global - 1 km)

processing: Country-driven product following the GSOCseq technical manual (v1.1). Countries, or the GSP for gap-filled countries, run a SOC turnover model on agricultural land using national or default inputs (SOC baseline, land cover/use (default ESA CCI), clay content, climate (e.g. TerraClimate)), for BAU and three SSM scenarios over 20 years. For Algeria the v1.1 report lists the layer source as 'Gap-filling Layer' with no national experts named.
validation: No independent validation for Algeria is reported; uncertainty layers are provided. The v1.1 report tables list Algeria among the NENA countries with the highest total relative sequestration rates under SSM3, with map source 'Gap-filled'.
limitations: Covers only current agricultural land; most of Algeria (non-agricultural land, Sahara) has no values.
Algeria is gap-filled by the GSP, not a national submission; inputs are global defaults, so results are indicative.
Scenario projections assume uniform percentage increases in carbon inputs; they show potential, not achievable or observed sequestration.
Licence information in the FAO catalogue is inconsistent (CC BY-SA / CC BY-NC-SA / CC BY across records).

Version labelling is inconsistent: the technical report describes v1.1 (2022), while the 2025 global 1 km catalogue records state edition 'Version 2.0'; the GeoTIFFs in the FAO bucket are dated 2024-01-21.
version: GSOCseq v1.1 (technical report, 2022); FAO catalogue global 1 km records labelled 'Version 2.0' (2025-01-07)

algeria_notes: Values exist only for agricultural pixels in northern Algeria (about one in five 1-degree grid points north of 32 N). Algeria was gap-filled by the GSP. Use as an indicative, scenario-based screening layer for cereal and agro-pastoral zones, not as an estimate of achievable sequestration.

verification.notes: Algeria coverage was checked by sampling the T0X and RSR SSM2 GeoTIFFs on a 1-degree grid and over a northern Algeria window (37.6% of 1 km pixels valid in -2..9 E, 34..37 N). published_date is the Crossref date of the v1.1 technical report (2022-03-21); updated_date is the 2025-01-07 publication date of the 'Version 2.0' global 1 km catalogue records. The report table layout is garbled in text extraction; one global table appears to list Algeria as 'National Submission', which contradicts Annex A3 ('Gap-filling Layer') and the NENA tables ('Gap-filled'). The annex is taken as authoritative.
